metadata.title: About — AVS
metadata.description: The mission, values and team behind the African visual standard.

manifesto.title: African visual heritage
manifesto.subtitle: As rigorous as Unicode is for writing. We're building it.

problem.label: The situation
problem.title: The richest visual heritage
problem.paragraph1: Every designer looking for an African pattern lands on the same libraries of images without source, without context, without clear permission. The same wax circulates without knowing where it comes from, nor who created it.
problem.paragraph2: There is no shared nomenclature, no reference palette, no token, no standard. Result: visual inconsistency, involuntary appropriation, and artisanal knowledge that fades generation after generation.

response.label: Our response
response.title: African Visual System is not a library.
response.subtitle: Seven interconnected bricks, each documented, versioned and traceable to its source.

method.label: Our method
method.title: How a pattern becomes a standard
method.researchDetail: Fieldwork, interviews, mapping of existing patterns.
method.validationDetail: Review by the source community — right of veto.
method.designTokensDetail: Colors, curves, spacings extracted and named.
method.componentsDetail: Figma, Tailwind, React integration — ready to use.
method.publicationDetail: Online publication, clear license, full traceability.

ethnographicRigor.title: Ethnographic rigor
ethnographicRigor.text: Each pattern is validated by field artisans and specialized researchers. No romanticization, no appropriation: factual documentation.

culturalSovereignty.title: Cultural sovereignty
culturalSovereignty.text: Source communities have permanent oversight over their heritage. AVS is a preservation tool, never an extraction tool.

universalAccess.title: Universal access
universalAccess.text: Most resources are free and open (CC BY 4.0). African knowledge belongs to all humanity, starting with Africans.

traceability.title: Total traceability
traceability.text: Each color token, each pattern, each symbol carries the trace of its source: artisan, region, era, documented meaning.

stats.label: Where the standard stands
stats.title: Two years of fieldwork, in numbers

countries.label: Countries represented
countries.detail: Out of 54 countries on the continent

roadmap.label: Roadmap 2024–2029
roadmap.title: From Douala to continental standard
roadmap.subtitle: Launched in 2024 from Bonamoussadi, Douala — two years of fieldwork before the first public line of code. Here is the plan, phase by phase.

01.title: Research & scoping
01.objective: Understand the real need before coding anything.
deliverables: Interviews with artisans and researchers to map existing patterns
Ethnographic watch on African classification systems
First technical prototypes — SVG formats, token structure
Definition of the data model and standard architecture

02.title: v1.0 launch
02.objective: Release a solid, documented, production-ready foundation.
deliverables: Open library of documented patterns
Figma & Tailwind integrations
Artisan verification system (v1)
Public documentation of the standard

03.title: Consolidation
03.objective: Solidify quality and governance before accelerating.
deliverables: Partnerships with museums and universities in Central Africa
Public API for third-party integrations
Strengthened artisan certification program
First recurring revenue — licenses and partnerships

04.title: Regional expansion
deliverables: Coverage of West Africa and Southern Africa
Community governance — artisan advisory committee
Multilingual translation program of the standard
Designer tools — plugin, CLI, stable API

05.title: Reference standard
05.objective: Become the continental reference, recognized and adopted.
deliverables: 54 countries covered, open and transparent governance
Adoption by major cultural institutions
Sustainable funding model
Official certification « AVS Verified »

team.label: Heritage guardians
team.title: Faces behind the standard
team.subtitle: A distributed team across the continent, united by the same conviction.

amara.name: Dr. Amara Diop
amara.quote: A pattern without its source is just decoration. Our work always starts with the name of the village.

ngozi.name: Ngozi Okonkwo
ngozi.quote: A standard is only useful if designers adopt it without thinking. That's our requirement.

jeanPaul.name: Jean-Paul Kamdem
jeanPaul.quote: Every token we publish must be auditable in twenty years. We build to last.

aicha.name: Aïcha Ben Salah
aicha.quote: North Africa is often absent from the continent's visual narratives. We correct this, pattern by pattern.

thabo.name: Thabo Mokoena
thabo.quote: Sankofa: go back and fetch what you left behind. That's literally our mission.

vision.label: Vision
vision.title: In twenty years, this standard will be as obvious as Unicode is today.
vision.subtitle: Each pattern integrated today protects a practice, an artisan, a memory. AVS does not exist to freeze heritage — it exists for it to continue to be created, transmitted and recognized, generation after generation.

metadata.title: Offer Me a Coffee — Buni
metadata.description: Support open-source projects and creative work. Every contribution fuels creativity and independence.

hero.title: Every coffee fuels
hero.description: Every project, every idea and every hour spent creating is made possible thanks to people like you. Your support means much more than a coffee.

ritual.label: THE RITUAL
ritual.title: Offering coffee has always meant something more.
ritual.paragraph1: Long before it became a gesture on the internet, offering coffee was an act of welcome — shared in courtyards, passed from hand to hand, a quiet way of saying you matter to me. Across the continent, from Ethiopian buna ceremonies to family compounds in Cameroon, coffee has never just been a drink. It's an invitation to sit down, to be seen, to belong.
ritual.paragraph2: When you offer a coffee here, you're taking part in that same tradition — encouraging someone who has chosen to spend their time honoring African heritage through design and code, one pattern, one pixel, one idea at a time.
ritual.imageAlt: Two hands sharing a cup of coffee, a gesture of hospitality rooted in African tradition

openSource.title: More open-source projects
openSource.text: Building tools and libraries that empower developers worldwide.

content.title: Better content
content.text: Creating tutorials, guides, and resources to share knowledge.

independence.title: Independence
independence.text: Staying free to create without external pressure or constraints.

heritage.title: A voice for African heritage
heritage.text: Keeping African design, patterns and stories at the center — not an afterthought.

whyAfrica.label: THE WHY
whyAfrica.title: Because Africa deserves to be told with care.
whyAfrica.paragraph1: Behind every kente pattern rebuilt in code, every ndop motif turned into a design token, there's a choice: to treat African heritage as a living, evolving language — not a decoration borrowed for a moment. That choice takes time, research, and care that isn't always visible on the surface.
whyAfrica.paragraph2: Your coffee doesn't just fund a feature. It tells someone working to put African craft on the same stage as any global design system: keep going, this matters.
whyAfrica.imageAlt: Close-up of a hand-woven African textile pattern, source of inspiration for the design system

contribution.title: Every contribution matters

explanation.pillar1: Documentary rigor — each resource carries its source, region, era.
explanation.pillar2: Cultural sovereignty — source communities retain permanent oversight.
